description: Integrate the selected n1024 eight-CTA global-workspace Sturm/inverse solver, compacted resident reorthogonalization and Rayleigh updates, triangular-inverse 256-column tensor-core WY path, and dead-kernel cleanup onto the accepted six-size candidate; preserve its n512 direct triplet/tail fold, n2048 active-rank reflector pulls, exact reducer bounds, strict correction passes, mapped classifier, certificates, hard-shape fallbacks and CUDA guards, then profile all six custom sizes and tune only integration-induced overhead.

Merged the selected eight-CTA n1024 global-workspace Sturm/inverse solver, compacted resident reorthogonalization with fused Rayleigh updates, 256-column triangular-inverse tensor-core WY path, and dead-kernel cleanup onto the accepted six-size candidate through the shared ancestor. The merge preserves the first parent's n512 direct triplet/tail-fold implementation and n2048 active-rank reflector pulls unchanged. Build and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean improves 30531.873 to 29942.991 us; dense n1024 measures 38938.112 us versus 41253.952 us on the second parent, while fixed stress fallbacks remain accepted.

Moved the fused n1024 reorthogonalization and Rayleigh shared arrays inside the compile-time fused branch so the common n512 tridiagonal_eigh_global instantiation no longer reserves n1024-only static shared storage. Build, kernelguard, and all 39 validations pass. Full geomean is statistically unchanged at 29943.544 us versus 29942.991 for the initial merge; dense n1024 is 38953.695 us versus 38938.112, while the noisy dense n512 term moves 86669.919 to 86585.307 us. The specialization preserves all numerical paths and isolates integration-only resources.

Integrated both parents in merge commit 7ccfad8c5762f98ef1e9c9efc07e977cc8ea06e6 and retained the clean specialization at 0bd5cbe64394d9e4c29a9b8cb6cbdf5b7801decc. The selected n1024 eight-CTA global Sturm/inverse solve, compacted resident reorthogonalization and fused Rayleigh updates, 256-column triangular-inverse tensor-core WY path, and dead-kernel cleanup now coexist with the accepted n512 direct triplet/tail fold and n2048 active-rank reflector pulls. Both trials build, pass kernelguard, and pass all 39 validations. Best full metric is 29942.991 us and final repeat is 29943.544 us versus parent 30531.873; dense n1024 is 38938.112/38953.695 us versus second-parent 41253.952. Moving fused-only shared arrays inside the compile-time branch leaves the score unchanged while removing n1024-only storage from n512. Final nsys captures for n32/n176/n352/n512/n1024/n2048 end in the final SHA; n1024 shows reducer 27.468 ms, fused solve/reorth/Rayleigh 3.484 ms, TRSM 0.673 ms, and no repair, while untouched routes match the accepted parent within noise. Keep the work moving through a custom SM100 triangular inverse plus V*T fusion to replace 16 TRSM launches, TMA/shared staging for 256-column WY panels, warp-shared Sturm recurrences across neighboring eigenvalues, or a persistent cluster schedule overlapping factor-workspace traffic with inverse iteration; identity/workspace reuse can also probe the remaining host/API launches without changing certificates or fallbacks.
